findings.issue: MAX_SESSION_COUNT caps handsPlayed and nextBotId, but nextBotName is still only checked as a safe integer >= 0. A stored record with nextBotName at or near Number.MAX_SAFE_INTEGER passes parseSessionRecord, so findPausedSession offers it and restoreSession seats it. In a cash game, the first bot bust calls nextReplacementName, which returns next = p + 1. That value is above MAX_SAFE_INTEGER, so the next bust's replacementName throws RangeError inside nextHand during play, not at the validation boundary. This is the same integer-overflow class SPEC-08 closes for the other two counters.
findings.evidence: IndexedDB sessions value (untrusted on resume) -> hand-store.pausedSession -> findPausedSession/parseSessionRecord (whole(record.nextBotName, 'nextBotName', 0), no max) -> App.resume -> restoreSession -> useTableSession -> nextHand -> nextReplacementName/replacementName throws 'Name position must be a whole number of at least 0'. Result: a resumed table stops mid-session after a bust. Only a local actor who can already write the origin's IndexedDB can trigger it, and it gives no information or privilege gain, so it is defence in depth.
findings.fix: Use whole(record.nextBotName, 'nextBotName', 0, MAX_SESSION_COUNT) and add a case to SPEC-08's rejection tests.

summary: I found no BLOCKER or MAJOR issues. Every value read from the sessions store goes through parseSessionRecord in findPausedSession, and restoreSession parses it again before the Table mounts. Those checks cover the session id regex, ISO dates including the new endedAt, config, seat kinds and styles against the config, names, the botId range and uniqueness, the chips via assertChips, and the new MAX_SESSION_COUNT cap. Invalid records are collected and logged with RangeErrors that carry field names only, never record contents; read failures make Home show no Resume entry. The Resume subtitle is built from validated numbers and enum labels and is rendered as React text, so there is no HTML injection path. A resumed session reuses the stored CSPRNG-format id, and new sessions still use crypto ids. There are no new dependencies and no network calls. One MINOR: nextBotName is not capped the way handsPlayed and nextBotId now are.
